newsitem.title: USA: NYC may raise size of next bond sale to $900 mln.
newsitem.headline: NYC may raise size of next bond sale to $900 mln.

text.p: New York City is considering selling up to $900 million of bonds in April, advancing and substantially raising the size of an offering planned for May, said Joe Lhota, budget director, on Wednesday.

The city had expected to sell around $300 million of bonds in May, but now is weighing increasing the offering by selling refunding bonds to save interest costs, he explained in an interview with Reuters Financial Television. The interview will be broadcast Thursday at 1515 EST/2015 EST.

"I'm not sure the underwriters have fully determined the size and extent of that, but it's quite possible we would move the bond issue earlier, into April, at this time, so that we would be able to use it for new money and a refunding, to take advantage of the current market environment," Lhota said.
He added that the approximate size of the offering was about $800 to $900 million.
